finding: The browser posted credentials to /api/admin/login and that shared app server called Supabase signInWithPassword. Supabase therefore applied its per-IP token bucket to the shared server egress and rejected the33rd burst request.
correction: The server still verifies the legacy password, creates or links the Auth user when required, and returns only auth_ready plus authorized admin context.
The browser now calls Supabase signInWithPassword directly inside the existing account-transition lock, so normal login and refresh traffic uses the user's network IP.
A429 is reported as a network throttle and does not increment the bad-password lockout counter.
No permanent Supabase rate-limit increase was made; rate_limit_verify remains30.
remaining_proof: Deploy an accepted candidate and run a distributed-origin login test. A legitimate shared network can still reach Supabase's intentional per-IP limit and should receive the new retry message.
